A2 Hosting is now hosting.com. The company announced the new name in April 2025, and a2hosting.com now points to hosting.com. People still search for "A2 Hosting", so this page covers the same host under its new name. The first-year price is very low, but the renewal is much higher. This page puts the prices, the renewal costs, the test results and the setup steps in one place. Prices were read from hosting.com's pages and a November 2026 catalog review on 20 November 2026.

Is A2 Hosting (hosting.com) worth it? The short version

  • A2 Hosting is now hosting.com. The plans are sold under the hosting.com name.
  • A very low first-year price. Starter is $1.49 a month on a 12-month term in the Black Friday offer.
  • A big renewal jump. Starter renews at $13.99 a month, 9.4 times the offer price.
  • Good speed in tests. HostingAdvice measured a 579 ms Largest Contentful Paint on a cheap plan.
  • The refund window is 30 days. A2's older anytime guarantee is gone.

What happened to A2 Hosting?

World Host Group bought A2 Hosting in January 2025. The company then renamed it hosting.com. Its own blog post says "A2 Hosting is now hosting.com". The old plan names changed too: Startup became Starter, Drive became Plus, Turbo Boost became Pro and Turbo Max became Max. If you are an A2 customer, your account and your plan now sit under hosting.com. The managed WordPress plans are built on Rocket.net, which joined the group in August 2025, according to HostDecider.

How much does A2 Hosting (hosting.com) cost?

hosting.com sells three shared plans and four managed WordPress plans. The shared prices below are the 12-month Black Friday prices read from hosting.com's plan catalog by ScaleHostReview (updated 20 November 2026). The regular price is also what the plan renews at.

Shared planSitesStorage12-month price a month48-month price a monthRenews at, a month
Starter515 GB NVMe$1.49$1.99$13.99
Pro1050 GB NVMe$3.49$3.49$19.99
Max50100 GB NVMe$5.99$6.99$27.99

Month to month has no discount: Starter is $13.99 from the first month. Before the sale, HostDecider (5 October 2026) listed the 48-month prices as $1.99, $3.79 and $7.79, so prices moved with the offer. The full term is charged at checkout.

The Black Friday FAQ on hosting.com says the deals run from 2 November to 14 December 2026. The plan catalog says 1 November to 1 December. The two pages disagree, so check the live offer before you pay.

[[cta: See hosting.com plans | A 30-day money-back guarantee applies. Check the regular price in your cart.]]

What does A2 Hosting cost after the first year?

The renewal price is the regular price, and it is the same whichever term you pick. This table is our own arithmetic from the prices above.

Shared planRenewal is this many times the 12-month priceRenewal is this many times the 48-month priceFive years: 48 months plus 12 months at the regular priceAverage a month
Starter9.47.0$263.40$4.39
Pro5.75.7$407.40$6.79
Max4.74.0$671.40$11.19

Starter's five-year figure is $95.52 for 48 months at $1.99, plus $167.88 for 12 months at $13.99. HostDecider quotes a real example: a Starter first year of $35.88 followed by 12 months at $143.88, a rise of 301%. HostDecider also notes that subscriptions renew automatically, and a saved payment method may be charged three days before the renewal date. Cancel before then if you plan to move.

What do you get with hosting.com shared plans?

  • Starter: 5 websites, 15 GB NVMe, an AI website builder for WordPress, email and security, a free domain for the first year, malware detection and removal, free managed migration, free SSL and daily backups.
  • Pro: everything in Starter, with 10 websites, 50 GB, more CPU and RAM, staging sites, preview URLs and Node.js support.
  • Max: everything in Pro, with 50 websites, 100 GB, 40 mailboxes, a service level agreement, a premium SSL certificate and priority support.

What are the managed WordPress plans?

hosting.com also sells managed WordPress plans. They are tuned for WordPress, with a Cloudflare Enterprise CDN, WP Rocket, two firewalls and a 99.99% uptime guarantee, according to WPThinker. Object Cache Pro is included from Medium up.

WordPress planSitesStorageVisits a month12-month price a monthRenews at, a month
Small120 GB30,000$4.49$9.99
Medium550 GB120,000$4.99$17.99
Advanced15100 GB250,000$10.99$25.99
Turbo50200 GB500,000$14.99$34.99

Medium costs only 50 cents more than Small in the first year, but it renews $8 a month higher. If you have one site, Small has the lower renewal. A 36-month term lowers the first price, to $3.49 for Small and $3.99 for Medium, according to HostDecider.

Is A2 Hosting good for WordPress?

Yes for small sites and for people who want managed WordPress. WordPress runs on every plan with one-click install. The managed plans add caching and security tuned for WordPress. If you want WordPress set up and kept running for you, our website maintenance service covers updates, backups and speed checks on any host.

How fast is A2 Hosting (hosting.com)? What independent tests found

We did not run our own speed or uptime test. Independent teams tested hosting.com. Their methods differ, so we list each.

TestResult
HostingAdvice, updated 12 November 2026. Two weeks, GTmetrix, live chat tests579 ms Largest Contentful Paint on the cheap plan. An A grade on WordPress hosting. Live chat replies in seconds
CNET, updated 2 October 2026. The reviewer bought a plan, built a site and tested supportFast, reliable servers and solid pricing. Setup was complicated and support was poor
Website Planet. WordPress Plus plan in Dallas, Divi test site, GTmetrix from Chicago, UptimeRobot for more than three weeksPages loaded in 0.8 to 2.2 seconds, an A grade on GTmetrix and 100% uptime. About 1 second slower in Singapore and 1.5 seconds slower in Australia

The pattern is mixed. Speed and uptime test well, but the experience reviews are less happy. HostingAdvice says the 99.9% uptime is a stated guarantee, not a measurement. Google treats a Largest Contentful Paint of 2.5 seconds or less as good, and 579 ms is far under it. Use the 30-day guarantee to check speed on your own site.

[[cta: Test it on your own site | You have 30 days to check speed and support and cancel for a refund.]]

How is hosting.com support?

  • Channels: 24/7/365 support.
  • What reviewers say: HostingAdvice found live chat replies in seconds. CNET found support poor and setup complicated, and it recommends hosting.com only for experienced site owners.

Is the A2 Hosting money-back guarantee still real?

Yes, but it is 30 days now. hosting.com's guarantee covers new purchases of shared, WordPress, email and reseller hosting. It does not cover domain registrations, renewals, VPS plans, dedicated servers, SSL certificates or third-party products. If you cancel, hosting.com refunds the hosting fees and takes off any domain fee. A2 Hosting used to advertise a longer anytime guarantee, so read the current terms fresh.

How do you cancel A2 Hosting?

Contact support within 30 days of buying if you want a refund. Outside that window, cancel before the renewal date, because plans renew automatically and a saved payment method may be charged three days before it.

A2 Hosting (hosting.com) pros and cons

Pros

  • The lowest first-year price among the hosts we compare.
  • 5 sites and daily backups on the cheapest plan, with free managed migration.
  • Good speed in HostingAdvice and Website Planet tests.
  • Managed WordPress plans with a CDN and a 99.99% uptime guarantee.
  • An AI website builder and an MCP server.

Cons

  • The renewal is 4.7 to 9.4 times higher on shared plans.
  • The sale price needs a 12-month or longer term.
  • CNET calls setup complicated and support poor.
  • The refund window is only 30 days, down from A2's older guarantee.
  • Speed is slower in Asia and Australia.

hosting.com vs Hostinger

hosting.com StarterHostinger Premium
Sale price a month$1.49 (12 months)$1.99 (48 months)
Renews at, a month$13.99$10.99
Websites53
BackupsDailyWeekly
Refund window30 days30 days

hosting.com allows more sites and daily backups on the entry plan. Hostinger renews lower. Read our Hostinger review and see all options in our best web hosting services list.

Who should use hosting.com, and who should look elsewhere?

hosting.com suits: people who want the lowest first-year bill, several small sites on one plan, and managed WordPress tuned by specialists.

Look elsewhere if: you want a low price for years, you are a beginner who wants easy setup and strong support, or most of your visitors are in Asia. Our DreamHost review and Namecheap review cover options with lower renewals.

How do you build a WordPress site on hosting.com? Step by step

  1. Choose shared or managed WordPress. Several sites and email: shared. One WordPress site managed for you: a WordPress plan.
  2. Pick a term and check the regular price. The renewal is the regular price, so write it down.
  3. Claim your free domain. It is free for the first year. Check what it costs to renew.
  4. Install or migrate WordPress. Use the one-click install, or ask for free managed migration if your site is elsewhere.
  5. Pick a theme and add pages. Add a home page, an about page and a contact page first.
  6. Use staging on Pro and above. Test updates before they go live.
  7. Set a renewal reminder. Cancel or change plans before the renewal date if the new price does not suit you.

Which hosting.com plan should you pick?

  • A blog or a few small sites: Starter.
  • More sites and staging: Pro.
  • Many sites and priority support: Max.
  • One WordPress site managed for you: WordPress Small, or Medium for up to five sites.

Final verdict: is A2 Hosting (hosting.com) worth it in 2026?

Yes for a low first-year bill, and no for a low price over many years. Starter's renewal is $13.99 a month, so plan to move or change plans after the first term. Use the 30-day refund to test it, and choose a different host if you want low prices for years.

Our interest in this topic

Reinforce Lab builds and maintains WordPress sites. We may earn a commission when you buy hosting through links on this page. We do not host our own site on hosting.com, so this is a research-based review. We read the host's pages and published tests, and we did not run our own. We do not sell hosting ourselves. How we researched this page is in the panel above.
